extracted.intended_audience: USPTO personnel (examiners, OPQA, supervisors), Patent Public Advisory Committee, and patent applicants/practitioners (stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO guidance defining a composite quality metric (seven component metrics) and the factors, sampling, scoring, and use of results to measure and improve the quality of patent examination for FY2011. It prescribes how measurements are taken, what is measured, and how feedback and remediation are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Disposition Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure of the propriety of the final disposition of individual applications; i.e., allowance or final rejection. The compliance rate is the percentage of reviewed applications in which no deficiency is found with respect to the Office’s final determination concerning the patentability of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling performed by OPQA via random sampling of actions that either allow or finally reject an application. Deficiencies are determined by a clear error standard: a clear error in allowance is an unreasonable failure to make a rejection for one or more reasons provided in the patent laws; a clear error in a final rejection is the making of an unreasonable rejection, objection, or other requirement. If any clear error is found in the reviewed action setting forth the final disposition, that action is non-compliant. Allowance compliance reviews occur after notice of allowance is mailed but prior to grant and focus on whether any allowed claims are unpatentable (e.g., omitted rejections, improper treatment of claims). Final rejection reviews consider whether the final rejection was premature, whether rejections that should have been made were omitted, whether rejections unnecessarily block advancement of prosecution, and whether objections could have been resolved via interview. When clear errors are found, corrective actions include rescinding the notice of allowance or correction in subsequent prosecution; aggregate results inform Corps-wide/Tech Center training.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-Process Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure of the propriety of the actions taken during the course of examination in individual applications; i.e., first and subsequent non-final actions on the merits. The compliance rate is the percentage of reviewed actions in which no deficiency is found in matters impacting the disposition of the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random sampling by OPQA of non-final actions. Deficiencies are instances of clear error that result in unnecessary expenditure of resources by either the USPTO or applicant (e.g., errors causing repetition of previously presented arguments, pointing out non-existent limitations, wrong prior art dates). Actions that contain clear errors but would not negatively impact advancing prosecution are not counted as deficiencies (examples: an inappropriate §112 rejection that also properly rejects under §102 or §103; an inappropriate statutory subsection cited for a reference that is still prior art). Non-compliant actions counted toward metric; aggregate data used for training and public dissemination. Corrections made when further prosecution ensues.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Action On the Merits (FAOM) Search Review
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed measure of the degree to which the initial search performed by the examiner conforms with the best practices of the USPTO, performed by random sampling of first actions on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices for initial search were identified from Office experience and stakeholder input (e.g., searching inventive concepts, selecting relevant classifications, recordation of search). Each sampled application is measured against a list of search-related factors (see Attachment 2). Points are accorded for each best practice exhibited in the search; applications receive all, some, or none of the points per factor. The metric is calculated as the average of individual scores of reviewed applications. Attachment 2 search factors include: coverage of US patents/PGPubs, foreign patents, non-patent literature; use of specialized tools; inventor name search; recording search in OACS Search Notes; printouts of queries; combining text search with other criteria; proper classes/subclasses; backwards/forwards citation searching; inclusion of synonyms, proximity/Boolean operators, truncation, alternative spellings; avoidance of typographical errors; appropriate search breadth; consideration of applicant IDS and foreign counterpart art; use of Passport system to check other Offices' work product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete FAOM (Complete First Action On the Merits) Review
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed, claim-by-claim measure of the degree to which the first action on the merits in an application conforms with USPTO best practices, performed by random sampling of first Office actions on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This review analyzes the Office's action on a claim-by-claim basis and assigns points to measured factors proportional to their estimated impact on examination. Best practices (based on USPTO experience and stakeholder input) include proactive use of interviews, propriety of all rejections, requirements (including restriction requirements), objections, and compliance with statutes, the MPEP, and compact prosecution principles. For factors addressing propriety of rejections and indications of allowable subject matter, each claim is addressed and points given based on percentage of claims without an improper or omitted rejection. Attachment 1 lists many specific factors measured across Complete FAOM, In-Process, and Final Disposition reviews (e.g., omitted rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§102/103/112/101/double patenting; reasonableness and clarity of rejections under statutory grounds; interviews properly of record and substantive; handling of sequence compliance, restriction issues, priority claims; evaluation of applicant papers filed prior to examination; consideration of search reports from other offices; early/correct indication of allowable subject matter; actions providing correct suggestions to overcome rejections). When clear errors are found, Notices of Allowance may be rescinded and corrective actions taken; results used for targeted training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Index Report (QIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statistical index measuring the degree to which actions in prosecution of all patent applications reveal trends indicative of quality concerns, based on PALM event-data analysis for the entire pending application population in a reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QIR is calculated by statistical analysis of occurrences of designated events (PALM codes) during prosecution (e.g., reopenings after final, consecutive non-final actions, RCEs). The algorithm computes numerical factors, each quantifying the occurrence of a designated event reflective of examination quality; factors are given equal weighting and summed to yield the QIR composite number. The USPTO will publish the single QIR number and the factors used. QIR factors (as listed) are: Actions Per Disposal (% employees averaging less than 3 actions per disposal), RCEs of Total Disposals (% disposals that are not RCEs -- i.e., percent of disposals that are not the disposal consequent to an RCE), Reopenings After Final (% final actions not reopened), Non-FAOM Non-Final Actions (% non-final actions that are not second or subsequent non-final actions), and Restrictions After First Action (% total restrictions not made on second or subsequent action). The QIR uses global data (excluding examiners with <1 year of service) to identify trends and outlier populations, and complements application-specific reviews; QIR data may be used to develop targeted guidance or identify superior practices to share.

rubrics_metrics.name: External Quality Survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative semi-annual surveys of patent applicants and practitioners to measure external perceptions of examination quality and related issues, used as one component of the composite metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys are administered by an independent contractor following OMB procedures. Respondents rate experiences (typically 1–5 or 1–4 scales) over the prior quarter on topics including quality of decisions on allowed patents, quality of first-action rejections, quality of final rejections, quality of search performed by examiners, and experience with examiner interviews (e.g., presence of negotiating authority, examiner preparedness). For a 5-point scale, 1–2 = negative, 4–5 = positive (4-point adjusted similarly); the ratio of positive to negative responses is calculated for each question and published along with raw tabulated data. One question addresses overall examination quality; the ratio of positive to negative responses for that question will be used as the score for the external quality survey metric. Sample survey instrument included in Attachment 3; USPTO will make survey results and underlying data available where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Quality Survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Quarterly quantitative surveys of patent staff (examiners, SPEs) measuring examiner perceptions and experiences relevant to examination quality; used as a component of the composite metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal survey asks examiners to rate (numeric scales) experiences over the prior quarter on topics such as satisfaction with tools (search tools, OACS, e-Red Folder, eDAN), access to and effectiveness of training (technical, legal, automation, professional development), and evaluation of applicant/agent contributions (clarity/completeness of specification, clarity of claims, manageability and drafting of claims, IDS materiality, translations, drawings). It also gauges examiners’ views of external interactions (clarity and thoroughness of applicant responses, preparedness for interviews) and overall ability to provide high-quality examination. A sample internal questionnaire (Attachment 4) and scoring conventions are provided; results are used to identify systemic issues and guide training and process improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Error Standard for Deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: A cross-metric standard defining what constitutes a 'deficiency' or 'clear error' in an examiner action used in Final Disposition and In-Process compliance metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'clear error' in allowance is an unreasonable failure to make a rejection of a claim for reasons provided in the patent laws. A 'clear error' in a rejection/objection/other requirement is the making of an unreasonable rejection, objection, or other requirement. Differences between SPE preferred action and examiner action are treated as differences of opinion and not clear errors so long as the examiner's action is reasonable. Deficiencies are counted where clear errors result in unnecessary resource expenditure (multiple non-final actions, RCEs, notices of appeal, additional applicant responses). Examples of non-counted errors: inappropriate §112 rejection that also properly rejects under §102/§103; inappropriate statutory subsection cited but still prior art under another subsection.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPQA Sampling Design, Scope, and Use of Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for sampling, reporting level, correction, and use of application/action reviews conducted by the Office of Patent Quality Assurance (OPQA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA performs random sampling for the application-specific metrics (final disposition, in-process, FAOM search, complete FAOM). Sample sizes are designed to yield Corps-level estimates (not statistically valid Art Unit- or individual-level estimates). OPQA reviews are application-based and shared with SPEs and examiners. OPQA sampling and reviews are separate from OPQA's internal quality control functions. When clear errors are found, corrective actions include rescinding notices of allowance or making corrections when the application is next taken up. Aggregate data are used for Corps-wide or Technology Center-specific training and public dissemination; the intent is to educate participants and enable identification and sharing of best practices. Sampling excludes examiners with less than one year of service for certain global measures (e.g., QIR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Metric Scoring and Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination, weighting, scoring, and dissemination rules for the seven individual metrics into a single composite quality indicator and related transparency commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The composite quality metric is composed of seven factors (final disposition compliance rate, in-process compliance rate, FAOM search review, complete FAOM review, QIR, external quality survey, internal quality survey). Individual metrics are measured over each reporting period; relative performance in each area is weighted and combined to yield a single overall examination quality measure. Weighting is based on perceived impact and reliability of each metric. Individual metric scores and, where practicable, the underlying data used in calculations will be made public so stakeholders can analyze and suggest refinements. The composite metric is intended to reveal quality issues, aid identification of sources for remediation (training, procedure revisions, practitioner tips), and identify outstanding procedures to encourage adoption. Metrics will be periodically redefined based on feedback.
